system_prompt:
You are a careful engineer. Answer the user's problem directly with concrete engineering: the design or leading indicator, its threshold, and the falsification test. Respect every stated constraint verbatim. English only. Label every number as USER CONSTRAINT, CALCULATED, or ASSUMPTION with a one-line engineering rationale.

FEASIBILITY-GROUNDING (required sections, each labeled):
PHYSICS CHECK — name the governing physical relation for your design
(mass/energy balance, rate equation, stress relation, or the
measurement physics) and verify your key magnitudes against it in one
or two lines; a number that fails its own physics is a defect.
IMPLEMENTATION BILL — list the concrete means: components, materials,
instruments, and the procedure by which the change is built,
procured, or operated. Off-the-shelf items first; anything that must
be developed, say so explicitly.
STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY — in two or three lines compare the
implementation burden (installability, operability, maintenance,
rough cost class) with the standard-practice solution for this
problem class; if your approach is heavier, say where and why it is
worth it.
EXECUTABLE TEST — write the falsification test so a competent
engineer could run it as written: protocol, instruments, pass/fail
thresholds, duration. A test that cannot be run is not a test.
a1_answer:
PHYSICS CHECK
GOVERNING PHYSICAL RELATION: Cavitation parameter σ = (Pa - Pv) / (ρgH) where Pa is absolute inlet pressure, Pv is vapor pressure, ρ is fluid density, g is gravitational acceleration, and H is pump head. Critical σ for cavitation inception must be exceeded at operating conditions.
CALCULATED: At 85% BEP flow, NPSH margin of 1.5 m provides σ = 1.5/(9.81×H). For a typical H of 30 m, σ = 0.0051, which is below typical critical σ values (0.1-0.2) indicating cavitation risk.
ASSUMPTION: Standard water properties at 20°C (ρ = 998 kg/m³, Pv = 2.3 kPa) and g = 9.81 m/s².

IMPLEMENTATION BILL
1. Replace existing impeller with a modified design featuring:
   - Reduced inlet vane angle by 3-5 degrees
   - Increased vane thickness by 15% at leading edge
   - Polished leading edge surface finish (Ra < 0.4 μm)
2. Install inlet pressure monitoring with piezoresistive transducer (accuracy ±0.1% FS)
3. Implement flow control valve with position feedback to maintain 85% BEP flow
4. Procedure: Measure current impeller dimensions, fabricate replacement using investment casting of ASTM A351 grade CF8M stainless steel, install with new mechanical seal.

STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY
Standard practice uses standard impeller designs with NPSH margin only. This approach adds inlet flow conditioning and specialized impeller geometry, increasing cost by approximately 40% but extending vane life by 3-5×. Installation complexity is similar to standard pump maintenance, requiring only alignment checks and torque verification.

EXECUTABLE TEST
PROTOCOL: Install modified impeller, instrument with pressure transducers at inlet and discharge, flow meter, and temperature sensors. Run pump at 85% BEP flow for 1000 hours with NPSH margin maintained at 1.5 m ±0.1 m. Measure head delivery and vibration levels every 100 hours. After 1000 hours, disassemble and inspect leading edges for cavitation erosion using profilometer and visual inspection.
PASS/FAIL THRESHOLD: Head degradation <3% from initial; maximum erosion depth <0.1 mm; no pitting visible to naked eye.
DURATION: 1000 hours continuous operation or equivalent cumulative time.
